fences.rule: A term that self-executes at its written formula and carries exactly its price drains and is there; a term whose exercise is renegotiated in the very state it was written for is here.
fences.case: Broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution bites in the down round at its formula and is almost never the object of a waiver negotiation, because it does not wipe the common.

fences.rule: The leaver's price fixed at entry and what the exit conserves are there; who the term actually bites when the state arrives and whose ledger decides it are here.
fences.case: A small seed fund in its eighth year sees its entire preferred position convert to common under pay-to-play because its reserves are gone, not because it stopped believing.

fences.rule: A price set for a reader who is not party to the trade is there; a refusal read before it is given, which discounts the outsider's bid on every secondary, is here.
fences.case: An outside buyer of an angel's shares bids as if the insiders had already matched every case worth winning, and the insiders may match at that discount.

fences.rule: Here pro rata is a call on the next round's information, worth nothing in a fund with no reserves left; there the empty reserve ledger is the fund state itself, with its motive for silence and the founder's cure by assignment.
fences.case: A seed fund whose whole return sat in the pro rata of two companies it could not afford to follow.

fences.rule: A most-favoured promise offered as a chip to break a deadlock, equality across time replacing advantage now, is there; the clause's bite as a multiplier on a later rescue's sweetener is here.
fences.case: A desperate company offers one rescuer a sweetener and the clause copies it to every earlier holder, so the rescue that needed one sweetener cannot afford the propagated one.

fences.rule: A term whose only bite is what it does to the founder's clock, making the search serial, is there; a term that carries a power in a future state is here.
fences.case: The term sheet's exclusivity period forbids running the raise in parallel for thirty days.
